50	   * @see {@link https://hono.dev/docs/api/hono#strict-mode}

76	   * })

100	  S extends Schema = {},
101	  BasePath extends string = '/',
102	  CurrentPath extends string = BasePath,
103	> {
104	  get!: HandlerInterface<E, 'get', S, BasePath, CurrentPath>
105	  post!: HandlerInterface<E, 'post', S, BasePath, CurrentPath>
106	  put!: HandlerInterface<E, 'put', S, BasePath, CurrentPath>

108	  options!: HandlerInterface<E, 'options', S, BasePath, CurrentPath>
109	  patch!: HandlerInterface<E, 'patch', S, BasePath, CurrentPath>
110	  query!: HandlerInterface<E, 'query', S, BasePath, CurrentPath>
111	  all!: HandlerInterface<E, 'all', S, BasePath, CurrentPath>
112	  on: OnHandlerInterface<E, S, BasePath>
113	  use: MiddlewareHandlerInterface<E, S, BasePath>
114	
115	  /*
116	    This class is like an abstract class and does not have a router.
117	    To use it, inherit the class and implement router in the constructor.
118	  */
119	  router!: Router<[H, RouterRoute]>
120	  readonly getPath: GetPath<E>
121	  // Cannot use `#` because it requires visibility at JavaScript runtime.
122	  private _basePath: string = '/'
123	  #path: string = '/'
124	
125	  routes: RouterRoute[] = []
126	
127	  constructor(options: HonoOptions<E> = {}) {
128	    // Implementation of app.get(...handlers[]) or app.get(path, ...handlers[])
129	    const allMethods = [...METHODS, METHOD_NAME_ALL_LOWERCASE]
130	    allMethods.forEach((method) => {
131	      this[method] = (args1: string | H, ...args: H[]) => {
132	        const methodName = method.toUpperCase()
133	        if (typeof args1 === 'string') {
134	          this.#path = args1
135	        } else {
136	          this.#addRoute(methodName, this.#path, args1)
137	        }
138	        args.forEach((handler) => {
139	          this.#addRoute(methodName, this.#path, handler)
140	        })
141	        return this as any
142	      }
143	    })
144	
145	    // Implementation of app.on(method, path, ...handlers[])
146	    this.on = (method: string | string[], path: string | string[], ...handlers: H[]) => {
147	      for (const p of [path].flat()) {
148	        this.#path = p
149	        for (const m of [method].flat()) {
150	          const methodName = m.toUpperCase()
151	          for (const handler of handlers) {
152	            this.#addRoute(methodName, this.#path, handler)
153	          }
154	        }
155	      }
156	      return this as any
157	    }
158	
159	    // Implementation of app.use(...handlers[]) or app.use(path, ...handlers[])
160	    this.use = (arg1: string | MiddlewareHandler<any>, ...handlers: MiddlewareHandler<any>[]) => {
161	      if (typeof arg1 === 'string') {
162	        this.#path = arg1
163	      } else {
164	        this.#path = '*'
165	        handlers.unshift(arg1)
166	      }
167	      handlers.forEach((handler) => {
168	        this.#addRoute(METHOD_NAME_ALL, this.#path, handler)
169	      })
170	      return this as any
171	    }
172	
173	    const { strict, ...optionsWithoutStrict } = options
174	    Object.assign(this, optionsWithoutStrict)
175	    this.getPath = (strict ?? true) ? (options.getPath ?? getPath) : getPathNoStrict
176	  }
177	
178	  #clone(): Hono<E, S, BasePath, CurrentPath> {
179	    const clone = new Hono<E, S, BasePath, CurrentPath>({
180	      router: this.router,
181	      getPath: this.getPath,
182	    })
183	    clone.errorHandler = this.errorHandler
184	    clone.#notFoundHandler = this.#notFoundHandler
185	    clone.routes = this.routes
186	    return clone
187	  }
188	
189	  #notFoundHandler: NotFoundHandler = notFoundHandler

100	 * @example
101	 * tryDecodeURI('Hello%20World') // 'Hello World'
102	 * tryDecodeURI('Hello%20World/%A4%A2') // 'Hello World/%A4%A2'
103	 */
104	export const tryDecodeURI = (str: string): string => tryDecode(str, decodeURI)

106	export const getPath = (request: Request): string => {
107	  const url = request.url
108	  const start = url.indexOf('/', url.indexOf(':') + 4)
109	  let i = start
110	  for (; i < url.length; i++) {
111	    const charCode = url.charCodeAt(i)
112	    if (charCode === 37) {
113	      // '%'
114	      // If the path contains percent encoding, use `indexOf()` to find '?' or '#' and return the result immediately.
115	      // Although this is a performance disadvantage, it is acceptable since we prefer cases that do not include percent encoding.
116	      const queryIndex = url.indexOf('?', i)
117	      const hashIndex = url.indexOf('#', i)
118	      const end =
119	        queryIndex === -1
120	          ? hashIndex === -1
121	            ? undefined
122	            : hashIndex
123	          : hashIndex === -1
124	            ? queryIndex
125	            : Math.min(queryIndex, hashIndex)
126	      const path = url.slice(start, end)
127	      return tryDecodeURI(path.includes('%25') ? path.replace(/%25/g, '%2525') : path)
128	    } else if (charCode === 63 || charCode === 35) {
129	      // '?' or '#'
130	      break
131	    }
132	  }
133	  return url.slice(start, i)
134	}
135	
136	/**
137	 * @deprecated
138	 * Use the `URL` API instead.
139	 */
140	export const getQueryStrings = (url: string): string => {
141	  const queryIndex = url.indexOf('?', 8)
142	  if (queryIndex === -1) {
143	    return ''
144	  }
145	
146	  const hashIndex = url.indexOf('#', 8)
147	  return hashIndex === -1
148	    ? url.slice(queryIndex)
149	    : queryIndex < hashIndex
150	      ? url.slice(queryIndex, hashIndex)
151	      : ''
152	}
153	
154	export const getPathNoStrict = (request: Request): string => {
155	  const result = getPath(request)
156	
157	  // if strict routing is false => `/hello/hey/` and `/hello/hey` are treated the same
158	  return result.length > 1 && result.at(-1) === '/' ? result.slice(0, -1) : result
159	}

161	/**

163	 * @param {string[]} ...paths - The paths to merge.
164	 * @returns {string} The merged path.
165	 * @example
166	 * mergePath('/api', '/users') // '/api/users'
167	 * mergePath('/api/', '/users') // '/api/users'
168	 * mergePath('/api', '/') // '/api'
169	 * mergePath('/api/', '/') // '/api/'

content.text:
The `strict` option is only read in one place: the `HonoBase` constructor. From there it has one effect, which is to choose the `getPath` function. No router looks at `strict`. Its effect reaches routing only through `this.getPath`.

## Declared and documented
- `src/hono-base.ts:46-54`: `HonoOptions.strict?: boolean`, with JSDoc `@default true` at line 52.

## Read and defaulted (the only place)
- `src/hono-base.ts:173`: `const { strict, ...optionsWithoutStrict } = options`. `strict` is pulled out so that `Object.assign(this, optionsWithoutStrict)` at line 174 doesn't copy it onto the instance. The instance never stores `strict`.
- `src/hono-base.ts:175`: `this.getPath = (strict ?? true) ? (options.getPath ?? getPath) : getPathNoStrict`
  - The default is `true`, applied by `?? true`.
  - With `strict: true` or unset, the app uses the user's `getPath` if one was given, otherwise `getPath` from `src/utils/url.ts:106`. That one keeps the trailing slash, so `/a` and `/a/` are different paths.
  - With `strict: false`, the app always uses `getPathNoStrict`. **A user-supplied `options.getPath` is silently ignored in this case.**

## The non-strict behaviour itself
- `src/utils/url.ts:154-159`: `getPathNoStrict` calls `getPath` and then removes one trailing `/` if the path is longer than 1 character (comment at line 157). The root `/` is left alone.

## Where the choice changes routing
- `src/hono-base.ts:420-421`: in `#dispatch`, `const path = this.getPath(request, { env })` feeds `this.router.match(method, path)`. This is the main effect: the normalised path goes to the router, and it also becomes `Context`'s `path` (line 424), which is what `c.req.path` returns.
- `src/hono-base.ts:367-372`: `mount()`'s default `replaceRequest` uses `this.getPath(request).slice(pathPrefixLength)` to rewrite the URL passed to the mounted app. With non-strict, the trailing slash is already gone before the prefix is removed.
- `src/hono-base.ts:178-182`: `#clone()`, used by `basePath()`, passes `getPath: this.getPath` into a new `Hono` without `strict`. The new app therefore defaults to strict, but it receives the already-chosen function, so non-strict behaviour carries over to clones.

## Places the option is passed through (no logic of their own)
These all hand the options object to `super(options)` / `HonoBase`:
- `src/hono.ts:26-27`
- `src/preset/tiny.ts:16-17`
- `src/preset/quick.ts:18-19`
- `src/helper/factory/index.ts:334-345`: `Factory` keeps `defaultAppOptions`, including `strict`, and `createApp` spreads the caller's options over them. A per-call `strict` therefore overrides the factory default.

The `strict` hits in cookie, proxy, jsx, secure-headers and ip-restriction are other features that happen to use the word and have nothing to do with this option.
